quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY3/2027 Results Briefing Q&A Summary (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kenichiro Fujimoto (results briefing Q&A, first quarter of the year ending March 2027): data-center businesses - UPS orders were strong in Q1, though the order pace fluctuates by the nature of the business; full-year UPS sales are expected, as initially assumed, at JPY 1,000 hundred million, up about 15% from the prior year. Full-year sales of optical devices for data centers are also expected in line with the initial assumption; for both UPS and optical devices the company aims for further upside by winning orders.
quarterly_data.figure: full-year UPS sales JPY 1,000 hundred million (about +15%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY3/2027 Results Briefing Q&A Summary (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kenichiro Fujimoto (results briefing Q&A): the full-year forecast was revised upward to reflect the first-quarter upside (FA systems above expectations and very high European air-conditioner demand; domestic air conditioners broadly as assumed). The initial assumption of JPY 150 to the US dollar was kept because the Middle East situation and government intervention could move rates sharply; if the current weaker yen continues from Q2 he expects an impact of about +JPY 1,000 hundred million on revenue and +JPY 300 hundred million on adjusted operating profit. The FX effect on adjusted operating profit was +JPY 220 hundred million in Q1, with -JPY 120 hundred million expected from Q2 onward. The special measures of the Next Stage support programme realised about +JPY 110 hundred million in Q1, about a quarter of the +JPY 450 hundred million annual assumption, while timing slippage at some affiliates had an impact of about -JPY 90 hundred million. The initial assumption of about JPY 60 hundred million negative impact from higher naphtha prices is unchanged (oil is below the assumed USD 100 per barrel). On the gap between price improvement and higher procurement costs in the full-year outlook: passing material price increases into product prices and booking them as revenue always lags, and the company's price improvement is not only pass-through of material costs but also includes better profitability at order intake.
quarterly_data.figure: FX sensitivity if the weak yen continues: revenue +JPY 1,000 hundred million, adjusted operating profit +JPY 300 hundred million; Q1 FX effect +JPY 220 hundred million

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY3/2027 Results Briefing Q&A Summary (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kenichiro Fujimoto (results briefing Q&A) on the earthquake in Kumamoto Prefecture: operations are restarting in stages, beginning with product testing (the final process) to minimise the effect on shipments; equipment suffered no major damage, but confirming safety before full production resumes takes some time. Damage appears smaller than ten years ago, at least as far as currently known: the Shisui plant in Kikuchi is new and only making samples, not in full production; damage at the Koshi plant is estimated at about one quarter to one third of ten years ago, when the whole power semiconductor business lost about JPY 80 hundred million, and is estimated lower this time. The impact is factored into the forecast under certain assumptions; seismic-isolation measures taken after the 2016 quake helped the faster restart.
quarterly_data.figure: Koshi plant damage about 1/4 to 1/3 of the 2016 quake (then about JPY 80 hundred million for the power semiconductor business)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY3/2027 Results Briefing Q&A Summary (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kenichiro Fujimoto (results briefing Q&A): talks with ROHM and Toshiba on integrating the power semiconductor business are continuing, including between top management, with nothing new to announce; no plan fixes what is decided by when, so the company does not see them as delayed. For the automotive equipment business with Hon Hai (Foxconn), due diligence and other procedures are under way while the two study how to create value through synergies for running a joint venture; early signing is not a priority. The definitive agreement is assumed within this fiscal year at the latest, and closing next fiscal year or later, with no detailed schedule fixed.
quarterly_data.figure: definitive agreement with Hon Hai within this fiscal year at the latest; closing next fiscal year or later

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY3/2027 Results Briefing Q&A Summary (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kenichiro Fujimoto (results briefing Q&A): strong FA systems orders are driven mainly by expanding AI- and semiconductor-related demand, a trend he expects to continue at least through this fiscal year - NC systems for machine tools in China are very strong, AI-related demand is lifting processing-machine demand in China, Taiwan and Korea, and semiconductor-memory-related demand for sequencers and servos is firm in Japan, China and Korea; China's growth is especially marked, Japan is growing too, and share is recovering in both. Some components show signs of procurement tightness, but standardisation of products and parts already in place should avoid the impact; if plans hold, further sales growth and higher profitability can be expected.

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY3/2027 Results Briefing Q&A Summary (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kenichiro Fujimoto (results briefing Q&A): Q1 air-conditioning results - Europe 109% of the prior-year quarter, both residential and commercial, helped by heat waves; North America 86% on a volume basis, with a recovery aimed for; Japan residential 113% and commercial 107% on pre-buying ahead of the energy-efficiency standard revision from fiscal 2027. Air to Water sales were up 10% year on year, not correlated with the heat, and are expected to stay strong; heat-driven residential demand is expected to settle from Q2 and is not built into the forecast.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 air conditioners: Europe 109%; North America 86% (volume); Japan residential 113%, commercial 107%; Air to Water +10%
